Compact and uncompact sets of cells

Source: R/compact.R
a5_compaction.Rd

a5_compact() stores a set of cells as an a5_covering: every complete group of siblings is replaced by its parent, repeatedly, giving the fewest cells for the same set, and the covering records the resolution the set stands for. a5_uncompact() expands coverings back to their cells at that resolution, or at a finer one. Uncompacting a compacted set returns the original cells, sorted in curve order and without duplicates.

Usage

a5_compact(cells, resolution = NULL)

a5_uncompact(x, resolution = NULL, simplify = TRUE)

Arguments

cells

An a5_cell vector. NA cells are skipped.

resolution

Integer scalar resolution. For a5_compact(), the resolution the covering stands for: by default that of the finest cell, and never finer than it. For a5_uncompact(), the resolution to expand to: by default each covering's own, and never coarser than it.

x

An a5_covering vector, or an a5_cell vector treated as one covering (see as_a5_covering()).

simplify

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), return one flat a5_cell vector with the cells of every covering concatenated in input order. If FALSE, return an a5_cell_list with one element per covering, suitable for a list column.

Value

a5_compact(): an a5_covering of length one. a5_uncompact(): an a5_cell vector, or an a5_cell_list when simplify = FALSE, with each covering's cells in curve order. A missing covering contributes no cells (an empty element in the list form).

Details

Both work on the index hierarchy (see a5_hierarchy), so the coverage they preserve is the set of index descendants, not a geometric area.

Memory

A covering can stand for far more cells than it stores: a country at resolution 18 is about a billion cells, stored as a few hundred thousand. a5_uncompact() refuses to build more than .Machine$integer.max cells; check with a5_covering printing first, and prefer the covering functions that work on compacted sets.

See also

a5_covering, a5_polygon_to_cells() and a5_grid_disk(), which return coverings.

Examples

cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 5)
children <- a5_cell_to_children(cell, resolution = 7)
covering <- a5_compact(children) # stored as the parent
covering
#> <a5_covering[1]>
#> [1] res 7: 16 cells (1 stored)
a5_uncompact(covering)           # the 16 children again
#> <a5_cell[16]>
#>  [1] 6314200000000000 6314600000000000 6314a00000000000 6314e00000000000
#>  [5] 6315200000000000 6315600000000000 6315a00000000000 6315e00000000000
#>  [9] 6316200000000000 6316600000000000 6316a00000000000 6316e00000000000
#> [13] 6317200000000000 6317600000000000 6317a00000000000 6317e00000000000

# expand to a finer resolution
a5_uncompact(a5_compact(cell), resolution = 7)
#> <a5_cell[16]>
#>  [1] 6314200000000000 6314600000000000 6314a00000000000 6314e00000000000
#>  [5] 6315200000000000 6315600000000000 6315a00000000000 6315e00000000000
#>  [9] 6316200000000000 6316600000000000 6316a00000000000 6316e00000000000
#> [13] 6317200000000000 6317600000000000 6317a00000000000 6317e00000000000

# one covering per element, kept apart with simplify = FALSE
disks <- a5_grid_disk(a5_cell_to_children(cell), k = 1)
a5_uncompact(disks, simplify = FALSE)
#> <a5_cell_list[4]>
#> [[1]]
#> <a5_cell[6]>
#> [1] 0cc2800000000000 0cc3800000000000 6314800000000000 6316800000000000
#> [5] 6317800000000000 631a800000000000
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <a5_cell[6]>
#> [1] 0cbf800000000000 0cc0800000000000 6315800000000000 6316800000000000
#> [5] 63be800000000000 63bf800000000000
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> <a5_cell[6]>
#> [1] 0cc0800000000000 6314800000000000 6315800000000000 6316800000000000
#> [5] 6317800000000000 63bb800000000000
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> <a5_cell[6]>
#> [1] 6314800000000000 6316800000000000 6317800000000000 6318800000000000
#> [5] 6319800000000000 63bb800000000000
#>
